meta.title: Bioorthogonally Cross-Linked Hyaluronan-Laminin Hydrogels for 3D Neuronal Cell Culture and Biofabrication.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: Hyaluronan-PEG hydrogels with covalently attached laminin were developed for 3D neuron culture and printed on a BIO X. Laminin stayed bound in the gel, and printed stem cells were about 50-55% viable.

formulations.review_notes: Viability reported as a range (50-55%); midpoint recorded. lt-NES species/source not captured.
formulations.name: 1% HA:PEG + laminin (click-crosslinked)
formulations.key_outcome: Laminin-presenting HA gels supported neuronal culture and could be printed at very low pressure.

evidence.quote: Bioprinting was conducted using a Cellink BioX equipped with a 27G needle at 1 kPa pressure and 25 mm s−1
Cell viabilities of about 50–55% were obtained with no difference between the two conditions
3D bioprinted structures based on the HA:PEG‐LN hydrogels at a concentration of 1% (w/v).
